newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Koreans hold back on grain/oilseed purchases.
newsitem.headline: Koreans hold back on grain/oilseed purchases.

text.p: South Korean grain and oilseed buyers are holding back on purchases after passing on a string of tenders due to higher-than-expected prices, dealers said on Tuesday.
They said the Korea Corn Processing Industry Association (KOCOPIA) was seen holding back on buying about 100,000 tonnes of U.S. corn for arrival in October.
Most South Korean flour millers would also probably put buying on hold this week due to strong wheat futures prices in Chicago, traders said.
One flour miller seeking about 17,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat since last week was expected to stay on the sidelines this week after prices climbed overnight on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT).
The July CBOT wheat contract closed on Monday seven U.S. cents up on the day at US$3.29 a bushel, largely on the back of rising corn and soybean prices.

The National Livestock Cooperatives Federation (NLCF) passed on a tender for 40,000 tonnes of soymeal, one day after a group known as the Big Feed Mills also passed on a tender for 30,000 tonnes of Brazilian soymeal due to high prices, dealers said.

The only action came from the state-run Agricultural and Fishery Marketing Corporation (AFMC), which bought 20,000 tonnes of U.S. No 1 soybean from Louis Dreyfus on Tuesday at $304.08 a tonne FOB and another 20,000 tonnes from Continental Grain at $326.54 a tonne C&F, traders said.
The first 20,000 tonnes will arrive by September 20 and the remaining 20,000 tonnes around October 20, both at the port of Inchon.
Further Korean purchases of Chinese corn to give to famine-stricken North Korea look unlikely, dealers said.
The AFMC said on Tuesday it did not have any plan to buy more corn to aid North Korea after it had bought 50,000 tonnes of Chinese corn for Pyongyang.
"We have no plan to buy more corn at the moment to aid the North," an AFMC official said.

On Saturday, the AFMC bought Chinese corn at $151.80 a tonne C&F from The Korea Express Co Ltd for delivery by the end of August to the western port of Nampo, near Pyongyang. Shipments will be made in lots of 5,000-10,000 tonnes each.
Traders said the corn was being bought from China because it is nearby and the need to transport the grain quickly.

On freight rates, an official with the Pan Ocean Shipping Co Ltd said rates for July shipments of Panamax-sized cargoes from the U.S. Pacific Northwest rose to between $13.50-$14.00 a tonne from $12.50-$13.00 last week.
Rates from the U.S. Gulf for Panamax-sized July shipments also rose to $24 a tonne from last week's $22 a tonne.
